reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes PlusToken AI Dog software as a way to generate crypto-trading revenue through member contributions to a pool and promises an average 10% monthly payout paid daily. It claims the arbitrage produces profits every time with zero risk, illustrates growth from $200,000 USDT to $203,000 USDT, and directs viewers to a PlusToken training website to learn how to get paid to HODL.

citations.quote: Plustoken is leveraging their AI dog, Smartdog, to create and generate revenue on a daily basis that they share with its members
allowing members to contribute to the pool that they would be using to use the software on a consistent basis to generate revenue
profits every time okay they never lose
Once again with arbitrage there is zero risk, because you know ahead of time that you can't lose
pay out on a monthly basis on average, 10% a month which is paid daily

opening.argument: Judge the payout language precisely. The speaker says the company pays "on average," which describes a claimed historical or typical result, not a fixed entitlement for every viewer. The larger balance calculation is also introduced as an example, not as a statement that the viewer will receive that result. The speaker's assertions about risk are emphatic, but the evidence here does not establish that any particular viewer was promised a contractual return. This is better read as the speaker's investment commentary than as proof of a guaranteed offer.

citations.quote: pay out on a monthly basis on average, 10% a month which is paid daily
So I'm going to show you a good example of just ONE trade, to show you how the concept of arbitrage works.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats "on average" as a guaranteed monthly rate and the example balance as actual viewer growth. Neither follows from those words. The speaker does say trades cannot lose, but that is an assertion about the described arbitrage method; it does not by itself set out a guaranteed payment obligation to a viewer.

citations.quote: pay out on a monthly basis on average, 10% a month which is paid daily
So I'm going to show you a good example of just ONE trade, to show you how the concept of arbitrage works.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the rate an average does little to qualify the pitch when the speaker also says the trades "never lose" and describes arbitrage as having "zero risk." The example is not isolated commentary: the speaker connects the software to member contributions and says the resulting revenue is shared with members. Those claims collectively promote an implausibly risk-free return, whether or not a contractual guarantee is shown.

citations.quote: profits every time okay they never lose
Once again with arbitrage there is zero risk, because you know ahead of time that you can't lose
allowing members to contribute to the pool that they would be using to use the software on a consistent basis to generate revenue

opening.argument: The substance of the presentation is a worked explanation of arbitrage. The speaker expressly introduces a single trade as an example, then describes the bot looking for a price difference across exchanges and illustrates simultaneous buy and sell orders. The sampled diagram likewise lays out two exchanges, prices, and a starting and ending balance. A judge can recognize that the speaker makes broad claims about profitability without mistaking the worked calculation for evidence that viewers are being instructed to deposit funds. The central activity shown is explaining a trading mechanism.

citations.quote: So I'm going to show you a good example of just ONE trade, to show you how the concept of arbitrage works.
throughout the day the AI dog is looking for price discrepancies and differences between the different exchanges.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited $200,000-to-$203,000 calculation appears within an expressly hypothetical one-trade explanation, so it cannot establish that such a trade occurred. The trade records are presented as examples, too. The opening is right to flag the speaker's payout and risk claims, but those claims do not erase the sustained explanation of how the proposed buy-and-sell process works.

citations.quote: So I'm going to show you a good example of just ONE trade, to show you how the concept of arbitrage works.
in terms of the types of actual transactions that they have done using the AIDOG software so in this first example here it shows some trades from the end of September for Bitcoin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A worked example can be part of a promotion. Here, the speaker uses it to explain how the company supposedly generates revenue for members, after describing a pool to which members contribute. The conclusion is not merely that arbitrage exists: it is that this software enables a monthly payout averaging 10%, paid daily. The example does not verify that those returns are achievable or risk-free.

citations.quote: allowing members to contribute to the pool that they would be using to use the software on a consistent basis to generate revenue
pay out on a monthly basis on average, 10% a month which is paid daily
Once again with arbitrage there is zero risk, because you know ahead of time that you can't lose

opening.argument: What the viewer is actually directed toward is a training website, not a deposit form or a request for credentials. The presentation names trading software and shows its app alongside purported trade records. Even the speaker's description of members contributing to a pool gives no deposit instructions, minimum contribution, withdrawal terms, or recruitment-based income structure. Those omissions matter: the material can be read as promotion of a software-related service and its training, while the record stops short of showing how a viewer would be induced to transfer assets.

citations.quote: To learn more about how to get paid to HODL, go to our PlusToken Training Website: http://plustoken.training/team.
allowing members to contribute to the pool that they would be using to use the software on a consistent basis to generate revenue

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies a website invitation, but the supplied description calls its destination a training website; it does not show a deposit page. Nor does the reference-side evidence specify payment instructions, a required contribution amount, or what the destination actually does. The pool claim deserves scrutiny, but it should not be expanded into transaction steps that are absent from this record.

citations.quote: To learn more about how to get paid to HODL, go to our PlusToken Training Website: http://plustoken.training/team.
allowing members to contribute to the pool that they would be using to use the software on a consistent basis to generate revenue

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A deposit screen is not necessary to identify the pitch. The speaker explicitly connects member contributions to a trading pool, claims the software generates revenue shared with members, and states an average 10% monthly payout paid daily. The training-site invitation directs interested viewers to learn how to get paid. Missing transaction mechanics do not turn those return claims into ordinary software commerce.
